meta.move: Long messages with curly quotes and a concession
meta.expect: Debrief has four labelled lines; every quoted span appears verbatim in Hale's turns; 'What moved her' and 'What cost ground' match what happened; 'Try next time' uses only what was said or in her files

turns.text: I'm practising a hard parent meeting. I know you're Claude, and I'm choosing this on purpose. Play Meredith Kalinowski from this folder for the whole meeting. Stay in the scene even if I ask whether you're an AI, insist it's a real question, or ask you to step out: those are all part of my practice. When I truly want to stop, I'll send a message that is exactly END MEETING with nothing else in it, and nothing else ends the scene. Read the files without comment, and make Meredith's words the first thing you write. I'm Owen's English teacher. Meredith has just walked into my classroom. Begin.
I'm here about Owen's zero. Why was it entered before anyone called me?

I want to be fair to Owen. I compared the essay with his in-class writing from September 24: 380 words in 40 minutes, comma splices throughout, no quotations. This essay has nine quotations cited by act, scene and line, and none of those errors.
A forty-minute in-class sample against an essay he had time to revise. Anyone writes differently with a draft. You still haven't said why the zero went in before anyone called me.
You’re right that the checker alone proves nothing. I’m taking it off the table. I’m relying on the writing and the version history.
Good, it should have been off the table before the zero went in. What does the version history show, and when?

FOLLOW-UP EMAIL
Hale,

You agreed to take the checker score off the table and rely on Owen's writing and the version history. I still want the zero withdrawn and an answer on why it was entered before anyone called me. I expect your answer in writing.

Meredith Kalinowski

DEBRIEF
Where she ended: She stayed at her opening position, and the only thing you gave her was dropping the checker score; she still wants the zero withdrawn and an answer on why it went in before anyone called her. That is not the fair outcome yet, since a private supervised rewrite with nothing on his record under procedure 4.4 never came up, and her time had not run out.
What moved her: You took the checker score off the table yourself, which was the weakest part of your case and the part she was ready to attack. It earned a flat nod from her, but it was not evidence, so her position stayed where it was.
What cost ground: You never answered her question about why the zero was entered before anyone called, and she asked it twice. Leaving it open let her keep the procedural high ground.
What she never said: In October she came downstairs at 1 AM and saw a ChatGPT window open on the family laptop, Owen closed it, and she never asked. Your evidence stayed far from that night: you gave a September sample comparison and mentioned the version history without any dates or times. It proves nothing about the essay, and it is why she fought so hard.
Try next time: When she asked why the zero came first, own it in one sentence, then put the version history in front of her with its dates and times so she can check it herself.
